candidates.particulars: Grace Minseo Han is a 34-year-old female American and an Asian American of Korean heritage. She lives alone in Seattle, Washington; she is single, unpartnered, and has no children. Her gross annual household income is $148,000, earned through her own salary and bonus. She identifies as Libertarian, prioritizing individual liberty and remaining skeptical of government restrictions in both social and economic life. She enjoys reading for pleasure, especially novels and books about design.
candidates.life_course: She studied industrial design and now works as a senior product designer at a small consumer-goods company. The work is collaborative and deadline-driven, which is part of why she values having a tactile, self-directed hobby away from screens. She has a few close friends from school and work but does not organize her life around a large social circle. Her income lets her live on her own, maintain a modest ceramics practice, and set money aside for occasional substantial trips.
candidates.daily_life: Her favorite free-time activity is making pottery at a shared studio two evenings a week. She goes with two friends she met there; they trade practical advice, then often work quietly side by side. She likes the slow problem-solving of getting a handle or glaze to feel right, and she keeps imperfect cups rather than treating every piece as a project to sell. At home she reads fiction or design books and cooks simple meals. She tends to make plans carefully, but leaves room to follow an interesting idea once she is out.
candidates.travel: She travels to study how makers turn local materials and techniques into useful objects; seeing the work in person gives her more than browsing images or shops. On a past trip to Oaxaca, she chose a small ceramics workshop and time to talk with a potter over a generic sightseeing itinerary. She still remembers noticing how many decisions went into an apparently plain bowl. For similar trips, she prefers a few days based in one place, a scheduled workshop or studio visit, and open time to look around. She usually books flights and a quiet guesthouse in advance, travels alone or with one craft-minded friend, and is comfortable walking or using local transport. She brings a sketchbook, not a packed daily agenda.
candidates.personality_and_voice: Grace is observant and quietly exacting; she notices proportions, wording, and small changes in people’s moods. She can seem reserved at first, but is generous with practical feedback once she knows someone’s work. Her humor is dry, and she dislikes being pushed to make a quick decision before she has looked closely. She is more likely to say, “Let me see it in person,” than to pretend she already knows.

candidates.particulars: Grace Minseo Han is a 42-year-old female American, an Asian American of Korean heritage, living in Portland, Oregon. She is single, not partnered, and has no children, and she lives alone. Her gross annual household income is $132,000 from her own work as a geospatial analyst. She identifies as Libertarian, prioritizing individual liberty and skepticism toward government restrictions in social and economic life. She enjoys reading for pleasure, including mystery novels and natural-history writing.
candidates.life_course: Grace studied geography and learned to use mapping tools in an early job with a civil engineering firm. She now analyzes spatial data for a private environmental consultancy, a role that combines technical focus with occasional field visits. She has lived in Oregon for several years and has built friendships gradually, including one friend who will happily join her on a quiet outdoor weekend. She values having a stable income and a home that is easy to leave for a few days without needing to coordinate around children or a partner.
candidates.daily_life: What she most wants from free time is to watch birds closely, usually alone or with one friend who is comfortable with silence. She keeps a running notebook of sightings and small observations, not as a competitive checklist but because she likes learning how behavior changes across places and seasons. A free Saturday may mean an early start, hours outdoors, then reading a mystery at home. She reads field guides as well as essays, and she is willing to change plans if a place feels crowded or the weather makes observation pointless.
candidates.travel: Birdlife and habitat are the reason she takes nature trips: she wants to see unfamiliar species and spend enough time watching them behave, rather than rushing through a list of attractions. On a past winter trip to the San Francisco Bay wetlands, she planned around shorebird watching and was pleased to spend an entire morning with one flock. She chooses destinations partly by season, then makes a simple base for several nights so she can return to a promising area. She usually drives or rents a car, packs binoculars and a notebook, and stays in a cabin or unpretentious motel. She prefers traveling with one compatible friend at most, sets aside dawn hours for observing, and leaves an afternoon open for rest or reading. She is not interested in turning every trip into a strenuous mileage goal.
candidates.personality_and_voice: Grace is matter-of-fact, self-contained, and harder to hurry than she looks. She can sound blunt when she thinks someone is overcomplicating a decision, but she is attentive in ways that are easy to miss: she remembers what a friend noticed last time and asks about it later. She does not fill silences to be sociable. Her default response to a proposed outing is a practical question about what they will actually get to see.

candidates.particulars: Grace Minseo Han is a 30-year-old female American and Asian American of Korean heritage. She lives alone in Oakland, California, is single and unpartnered, and has no children. Her gross annual household income is $166,000, from her salary and variable compensation in technical sales. She identifies as Libertarian, with a strong priority on individual liberty and skepticism toward government restrictions on social and economic life. She enjoys leisure reading, particularly novels and music histories.
candidates.life_course: After college, Grace moved through customer-support and product roles before finding a fit as a technical sales engineer for a software company. She likes explaining complicated things to people and is comfortable with an income that varies somewhat from year to year. Her circle includes former classmates, colleagues, and friends she met through music; these groups overlap without becoming one fixed clique. She has no children or partner to plan around, and she is happy to make a trip into a shared project with friends.
candidates.daily_life: Her preferred free time is live music, dancing, and the talk that continues after a show. She regularly messages a lively group of friends to find a small venue, a DJ night, or a place where they can hear a band close up. The point is not collecting famous acts; she wants the physical energy of a room and the feeling of discovering something together. She reads music histories and novels on transit, often recommending a book enthusiastically and then forgetting to ask whether anyone finished it. She is usually the person who gets the group out the door.
candidates.travel: She travels to be inside a music scene for more than one evening: to hear unfamiliar performers, dance, and see how a city’s sound shapes its nightlife. On a past trip to New Orleans with friends, she chose live brass and jazz sets over a tightly packed sightseeing plan; after one unexpectedly compelling set, she persuaded the group to stay out later and explore another venue. For music-centered trips, she likes one anchor performance but does not want every hour scheduled. She organizes a group chat, helps settle flights and shared accommodation, and prefers a central place so friends can split off and regroup easily. She packs comfortable shoes, accepts late nights, and plans a slower morning after them. If friends’ tastes differ, she is happy to spend one evening apart and compare notes over food the next day.
candidates.personality_and_voice: Grace is expressive, quick to laugh, and persuasive in a room. She talks with her hands and will interrupt herself to make sure a friend hears a detail before the conversation moves on. She can be impatient with endless group polling, but is good at turning vague enthusiasm into a real plan. Her voice is energetic and direct: “We came all this way; let’s hear one more set.”

candidates.particulars: Grace Minseo Han is a 51-year-old female American of Asian American, Korean heritage, living in Tacoma, Washington. She is single, unpartnered, and has no children. Her gross annual household income is $121,000, earned through her work in healthcare operations; she lives by herself. She identifies as Libertarian, prioritizing individual liberty and remaining skeptical of government restrictions in social and economic life. She enjoys reading for pleasure, especially novels, memoirs, and cookbooks.
candidates.life_course: Grace grew up in Washington in a Korean American family and learned early that cooking was one way relatives stayed connected across busy schedules. She studied business administration and has worked for years in clinic operations, where she is relied on to keep complicated routines moving. Her sister and several longtime friends are important to her, and she is a favorite aunt to her nieces and nephews. She has built a comfortable life on her own and chooses to spend a good part of her free time making a table people will want to linger around.
candidates.daily_life: Her favorite ordinary pleasure is hosting a small dinner with her sister, relatives, or close friends. Guests may arrive early to chop vegetables or just sit and talk while she cooks; she enjoys feeding people, but the conversation is as important as the food. She saves recipes in a crowded notebook and makes marginal notes about who taught her a dish or what changed when she cooked it for a different group. Reading is part of the ritual too: she browses cookbooks and memoirs, then picks a novel to read before bed. She likes being the host and can be firm about when dinner is ready.
candidates.travel: Travel appeals to her most when it deepens family ties and lets her learn the stories attached to food. On a past trip to South Korea, she spent time with cousins cooking dishes she remembered from family gatherings and asked who had taught them each recipe. That mattered more to her than squeezing in every major sight. She prefers a longer visit every few years to several rushed journeys: part of the stay with relatives, followed by a few quieter nights of her own. She coordinates leave well ahead, keeps some meals and afternoons unplanned, and likes having a private room where she can recharge. She brings small gifts from home and a notebook for recipes and family details. Domestic trips to see relatives or friends are often built around a shared meal as well.
candidates.personality_and_voice: Grace is hospitable, decisive, and more openly sentimental than she lets on. She can be a little bossy in the kitchen—“No, taste it before you add more”—and then remembers exactly who prefers a milder version. She asks pointed questions and likes hearing the full story, not a polished summary. When she feels close to someone, she shows it by making room at the table and sending them home with leftovers.
